title: Pushbutton (6 mm, 4 legs)
_note: Pin 1 is the first hole that you tap. row and col count rows and columns from pin 1. The two legs in the same column always connect, so they have the same name. A press connects pin 1 to pin 2. across: the part must go across the center gap.

datasheet.summary: A tactile switch with 4 legs. A press connects one side of the switch to the other side. It has no chip and needs no power. The real switch has no numbers on it: in Jumper, the legs of one side are named 1 and the legs of the other side are named 2.
datasheet.supply: No power pin. A logic input at 3.3 V or 5 V is safe. The rating is 3 V to 24 V DC, 50 mA maximum.

pins.1: Side 1. Its two legs always connect inside the switch. A press connects them to side 2. On the Omron drawing, legs 1 and 2 are one side.
pins.2: Side 2. Its two legs always connect inside the switch. A press connects them to side 1. On the Omron drawing, legs 3 and 4 are the other side.
